name: DaVinci Power Bins Preset Workflow
use_when: A Resolve editor repeats zooms, text animations, flashes, overlays, or adjustment-clip effects across projects.
The agent needs a reusable style system for short-form editing speed.
A custom effect has been tested and should become part of the editor's workflow.
avoid_when: The effect has not been checked for readability, crop safety, or timing.
The preset is project-specific and would mislead future edits.
Power Bins are already cluttered with unclear names or duplicate versions.

timeline_pattern.pattern: build_effect -> verify_phone_preview -> show_power_bins -> new_named_bin -> drag_effect_or_adjustment_clip -> rename_by_job -> reuse_in_new_project -> customize_text_color_timing
timeline_pattern.naming_rule: Name presets by job and motion, not vague hype.
timeline_pattern.business_rule: Presets increase speed and consistency, but they do not replace story, hook, or judgment.
timeline_pattern.reuse_rule: Any repeated text, zoom, flash, overlay, or LUT/style treatment should be considered for a reusable bin only after QC.

motion.rule: Save motion presets only after confirming they preserve vertical crop, captions, and focus.

sound.rule: If a preset includes SFX, keep the audio editable and low enough for dialogue-first use.

captions.rule: Caption presets should include safe-area and readability assumptions in the name or notes.

color.rule: Color or LUT presets should preserve skin tone and caption contrast before they enter the reusable workflow.

implementation.ffmpeg: Store reusable filter chains as named JSON/YAML snippets with required inputs, safe regions, and QC notes.
implementation.remotion: Create reusable components or preset objects with typed props for text, color, timing, and safe areas.
implementation.blender: Store reusable node groups, text rigs, and camera moves in asset libraries with descriptive names.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use saved templates, favorite effects, brand kits, and copied projects as reusable style systems.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use presets, Essential Graphics templates, adjustment-layer presets, bins, and project templates.

common_mistakes: Saving an effect as a preset before it is actually good.
Naming presets so vaguely that future agents cannot choose correctly.
Letting preset speed create repetitive, cookie-cutter edits.
Believing more effects or more hours automatically means more professional work.
qc: Was the preset checked at phone size before saving?
Does the preset name describe the job and motion clearly?
Can the preset be reused without hidden project-specific assumptions?
Does the preset preserve captions, faces, and proof in vertical layout?
Does preset use make the edit faster without making it generic?
